## Sleep Duration and Sleep Quality Changes
- **Sleep duration** was stable over the two weeks, averaging 454 minutes (approximately 7.6 hours) with a low standard deviation of 6.4 minutes. Daily durations ranged narrowly from 440 to 465 minutes, with no clear upward or downward trend.
- **Sleep quality** showed moderate day-to-day variation, with an average score of 64.4 and a standard deviation of 6.2. Scores ranged from 55 to 74, and no consistent trend emerged over the 14-day period.
- The relationship between sleep duration and quality was not strong. For example, on 2026-03-18, a duration of 450 minutes yielded a high quality score of 74, while on 2026-03-19, a longer 460-minute sleep resulted in a low score of 55.
- Notable high-quality nights included 2026-03-18 (score 74) and 2026-03-13 (score 73), while low-quality nights included 2026-03-19 (score 55) and 2026-03-17 (score 57). Even the shortest sleep duration (440 minutes on 2026-03-20) was accompanied by an above-average quality score of 69, underscoring the weak correlation.

## Premature Ventricular Contraction Events
- Throughout the entire two weeks (2026-03-11 to 2026-03-25), no premature ventricular contraction events were detected in any monitoring session. The PVC count remained consistently at zero, indicating no change or occurrence of PVC events over this period.
